input.brief: Prototech PCB construction becomes a large branded product exhibit, with a white logo and scroll-scrubbed exploded copper and FR4 layers inspired by the supplied video

direction.name: The object, large
direction.idea: Show the thing, bigger than seems reasonable. One photographed object fills the first screen, scaled until the viewport crops it, with the text small and tucked beside or behind it. The crop is the idea: a record whose edge leaves the top-right corner, a bottle whose shoulder runs off the bottom, a chair seen so close you read its grain. Being that close reads as confidence in the object. Everything else on the page serves it: details as tight close-ups, facts as short lines, one way to buy.
direction.composition: First screen: the object occupies 55–75% of the viewport and breaks at least one edge. It sits on a flat field (ground colour or one bold colour), never in a box. The headline is short and either very large and partly hidden behind the object (10–13vw, the object overlapping two or three letters) or small (28–36px) in the opposite corner with a one-line description. No navigation bar beyond a wordmark and one action. Following sections: a row of three or four close-up details at different crop ratios (not equal tiles), a single wide photograph of the object in use, a plain list of facts set large (materials, size, price) aligned to one edge, then the purchase action. The object returns once at the end from a different angle.
direction.typography: Either very large and structural or very small and precise; pick one for the headline and hold it. Facts are set in the text face at 22–28px, not in a table.
direction.colour: A flat field chosen to make the object's own colour sing (its complement, or a tone darker than its shadow side). One field for the whole page, or a second for the facts section.
direction.imagery: Use the product's own photographs if they exist. Otherwise use a still-life from the dealt set as a stand-in and say so. Prefer images with a plain background; use `mix-blend-mode: multiply` on light fields so a white studio background disappears into the page colour.
direction.photoTreatment: Scale the main image well past its container (`width: 120–160%`) and let `overflow: hidden` on the section do the cropping.
direction.richness: The object's surface at close range, and the tension of the crop.
direction.pitfalls: A small centred product shot with space all round is a catalogue thumbnail, not this direction. If the image has a busy background it cannot sit on a field; crop tighter or change image. Keep text off the object's focal area.

hero.name: Counter object, wide wordmark
hero.blueprint: Borrowed from a watch or perfume counter. One flat charcoal field. Centred slightly above the midline, a single low-key photograph of the object about 31% of the viewport wide (columns 5-8), 4:5, its own dark background matched to the field with filter: brightness(0.9) so it sits without a frame. Under it the name runs on one line as an ultra-wide wordmark spanning 72% of the width yet only about 45px tall: an extended face with letter-spacing near 0.6em, or a regular face stretched with transform: scaleX(2.4). Then one centred serif sentence at clamp(24px, 2.6vw, 38px). Then a single centred row at 15px with 48px between its three parts: one specification, the price inside the one solid light rectangle that is also the action, a second specification. The wordmark repeats small top-left and one text link sits top-right, both on 32px margins. The bottom fifth and both outer quarters of the screen stay empty and dark.
hero.mobile: The photograph grows to 70% of the width at 4:5, its top at 16% of the height. The wide wordmark spans the full width inside 20px margins at about 28px tall. The serif sentence sets at 6vw on two lines. The row stacks into three centred lines with the action in the middle at full width. The lowest sixth of the screen stays dark and empty.
hero.headline: The name as a very wide, very low wordmark on one line (up to 12 characters); the serif sentence beneath is the supporting line, up to 40 characters.

photos.title: Architecture
photos.note: structure, lines, bridges, facades and building interiors
photos.treatment: Scale the main image well past its container (`width: 120–160%`) and let `overflow: hidden` on the section do the cropping.

photos.alt: Red suspension bridge tower rising from fog above rugged cliffs
Small figure walking past a huge bright yellow wall
Tall pointed vaults and pale columns of a church interior
Green bicycle leaning against a weathered wooden shed with blue door
Underside of a red suspension bridge reaching toward hills in pastel light
Grand station concourse with arched windows and a blurred crowd
Gothic stone college building facing a striped green lawn

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Heading captions a panorama
sections.blueprint: The section is exactly 100svh. Its top third holds a two-line heading of three to six words at clamp(48px, 6.5vw, 96px) with leading 0.95, either centred or flush left on the page margin. 28px beneath the heading sit two small captions side by side, each two lines at 13px and 150px wide with a 48px gap, aligned to the heading (centred as a pair, or both starting at its left edge). 40px below them a full-bleed photograph begins and runs off the bottom of the viewport: it is 100vw wide at 21:9 or wider, and only its top 55–60svh is visible before the fold, the rest arriving with scroll. The heading therefore reads as a large caption to the picture. On an object-led page the image is the object on a flat dark panel inset by the page margin instead of bleeding to the edges.
sections.mobile: Heading at 12vw on two lines, left-aligned, taking the top 30% of the screen. The two captions merge into one four-line block at 14px. The photograph begins at 45% of the screen height in a 4:5 crop, full-bleed, and runs off the bottom.

sections.name: Specimens on colour tiles
sections.blueprint: Each capability is represented by one object photographed alone and shown on a flat colour tile. Columns 1–3 hold the heading (two to four words at 40–52px), top-aligned, with a 30ch sentence beneath and nothing else down the rest of that column. Columns 4–12 hold a grid of five or six tiles in two rows with 10px gaps: tiles are 4:5 except one, which is double width at 8:5 and placed second in the first row. Tile colours rotate through three palette fields. Each photograph is centred at about 70% of its tile's height; on light tiles use mix-blend-mode: multiply so a white studio background disappears. Under each tile, outside it and aligned to its left edge: the capability name at 20px medium and one fact at 16px in the soft ink. No text on the tiles and no hover lift.
sections.mobile: The heading and its sentence sit on top at full width. Tiles become a two-column grid with 8px gaps; the double tile spans both columns at 8:5 and comes first. Names shrink to 17px and facts to 15px, still under each tile.

sections.name: Two objects, two fields
sections.blueprint: Two panels side by side, each 50vw wide and 92svh tall, in two different flat tones from the palette, meeting on a clean vertical edge with no gap. Each panel is dominated by one cut-out object photograph scaled to 130–150% of the panel's width and positioned so the panel's top edge crops it: the reader sees the lower two-thirds of the object, very close. On light panels use mix-blend-mode: multiply to lose a white studio background. Along the bottom of each panel, 28px in from the edges, one row: the name at 20px medium and a price or fact at 17px on the left; on the right, two small rectangular actions, one filled with ink and one with paper. Nothing sits in the middle of a panel. The heading, two to four words at 32–40px, is set at the top-left of the first panel only, in the empty corner beside the object.
sections.mobile: Panels stack, each 78svh tall, the object scaled to 150% of the width and cut by the top and right edges. The bottom row becomes two lines: name and fact, then the two actions side by side at full width. The heading sits top-left on the first panel at 26px.

sections.name: Full-bleed sequence, text interlocked
sections.blueprint: Three photographs, each 100vw by 100svh, shown one after another with nothing between them. Each is `position: sticky; top: 0` inside a wrapper 300svh tall, so the second slides up over the first and the third over the second like a curtain; no scroll hijacking. The section above interlocks with the first photograph: a narrow paragraph at 13–14px, 220px wide, sitting on the column line at 58% of the width, is pulled down with a negative bottom margin so its last four lines overlap the photograph's top edge, in a colour that reads on both ground and image. Each photograph carries one caption line at 15px in white at the bottom-left margin, over a neutral dark scrim limited to the lowest 120px. No heading. Choose three frames with the same light and a calm lower-left corner. The last photograph releases into the next section.
sections.mobile: Each photograph is 100vw by 88svh in a portrait crop and still sticks so the next covers it. The interlocking paragraph sits at the left margin, 60% wide, overlapping the first photograph by three lines. Captions stay bottom-left at 14px.

sections.name: Names running off the edges
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed band in a flat colour, about 34vh tall, holding a single line of names that is cropped by both viewport edges. The names are set at 8vw in the display weight, `white-space: nowrap`, separated by a solid round dot one third of the cap height, and the line moves slowly to the left (a CSS `translateX` animation over 40 seconds on a duplicated track, paused under `prefers-reduced-motion`). The band has no heading. Its meaning comes from one sentence at 18px set directly below the band at the left margin on the page ground, stating plainly who these names are. Supplied logos may replace names if all are available as single-colour SVGs at 0.8em height; do not mix logos and set names in one line. The band butts against the sections above and below with no gap.
sections.mobile: The band is 22vh tall with names at 15vw, still cropped at both edges and still moving. The explaining sentence sits under it at 16px with 20px margins. Do not add a second line running the opposite way; one line is the idea.

sections.name: The action tile
sections.blueprint: The close is one row of the board. Three filled tiles sit side by side with 8–14px gaps, all 360px tall and sharing one radius: a wide centre tile spanning columns 3–10 in the accent colour, flanked by two narrow tiles (columns 1–2 and 11–12) that run off the left and right viewport edges, as if the row had been cropped from a longer one. The centre tile holds, left-aligned and vertically centred with 40px padding: a heading of three to five words at 40px, two lines at 17px, and the action. The action is either one rectangular button or an email field 420px wide in the paper colour with the submit button nested inside its right end. The flanking tiles hold no text: one is a photograph covering the tile, the other a flat palette colour. No shadows, no outlines.
sections.mobile: The accent tile runs full width, about 300px tall, heading at 28px, field and button stacked at full width. The two flanking tiles follow beneath as a pair, each half width and 120px tall, with the same gap and the same radius.

sections.name: Photograph half, menu half
sections.blueprint: A split footer one viewport tall. The left half is a single photograph filling columns 1–6 edge to edge, cropped hard by the left and bottom viewport edges: a close crop of the page's main subject, larger than it appeared anywhere above. The right half, on a flat field, is the site's menu set large: five or six section names stacked as links at about 2.6vw bold, 28px apart, starting at column 8 and 80px from the top. Rows are separated by space only; on hover a row's label shifts right by 12px and the others drop to the softer ink. Under the menu, 64px lower, two short blocks at 15px side by side: contact and social. The legal line runs along the very bottom of the right half at 12px. The wordmark sits small at the top of the right half, on the menu's left edge.
sections.mobile: The photograph leads at full width and 50svh, cropped tight. The menu follows on the flat field at 8vw per item with 20px between items, then contact and social stacked at 15px, then the legal line at 12px. The wordmark sits small above the menu.

references.name: starboy
references.idea: A tiny gadget shown enormous: product renders so large the screen crops them, wrapped around a nursery-rhyme headline in fat lowercase.
references.hero: No nav, logo or button. Off-white ground. The right half holds the headline: five stacked lines of very bold rounded lowercase at 13vw (187px), right-aligned and almost touching the right edge, with tight negative tracking and leading under 0.9, so the stack runs from 5% below the top to past the fold and the last line's descenders are cut off. The left 60% is one transparent-shelled, star-shaped device rendered at huge scale (yellow circuit board, round black screen), rotated and cropped by the top, left and bottom edges, its right-hand points tucking behind the letters. A chrome keyring loop peeks in at bottom-right.
references.type: Milling Triplex 1mm, bold, for the headline at 187px in lowercase with -0.055em tracking, one or two words per line over eleven lines; the same family at about 13px for body copy, product names and footer links, all lowercase. Two sizes only, a 14:1 jump.
references.colour: #f9f9f9 #2a2b2d #f5d900 #8d8e96 #b8a45c #2f6fe0 — Off-white page with charcoal type. Colour lives in the objects: circuit-board yellow, chrome, matte black, brass. A small blue logo in the footer is the only interface colour.
references.imagery: Photoreal renders of star-shaped devices in four materials, cut out with no background or cast shadow, scaled well beyond the viewport, each rotated differently and cropped by the edges. Accessories are shown small and centred in grid cells.
references.layout: Three acts: three screens of oversized renders tumbling diagonally with the headline set right, then left; one screen holding a single narrow text column and nothing else; then a three-column hairline-divided product grid running edge to edge with no outer margin.

sections.description: The second and third screens are only renders: a matte-black star and a chrome star overlap on a diagonal, each wider than half the viewport and cropped by two edges. The second half of the headline then appears left-aligned at the same 13vw, left of centre, while a brass star fills the right half and bleeds off the top and right. No captions or interface.

A single column of 13px lowercase text about 290px wide, placed roughly 15% from the left and starting at the top of the viewport: five short paragraphs, the first in medium weight. The remaining three-quarters of the screen is blank off-white. No heading, image or button accompanies it.

Three equal columns span the full viewport width, separated by faint 1px vertical and horizontal lines. Each cell holds one cut-out render centred with generous air and a caption row along its bottom edge: product name at left, price with stock count or a coming-soon note in grey at right, all 13px lowercase. The footer is one row: small blue logo left, five text links right.

steal: Scale the product until two or three viewport edges crop it, and let its silhouette tuck behind the headline letters.
Break a sentence into one or two words per line at 13vw, right-aligned for the first half and left-aligned for the second, so the headline spans several screens.
Follow a loud hero with one tiny text column on an otherwise empty screen; the drop in scale does the pacing.

references.name: ARCHIV
references.idea: A waitlist page as a museum plinth: one cut-out everyday object at a time, centred on off-white beneath a heavy serif wordmark.
references.hero: Off-white single screen with no scroll. A heavy high-contrast serif wordmark in black caps sits top-left at a 56px margin, about 410px wide (28% of the viewport) and 80px tall. Opposite, top-right at the same margin, one line of 14px sans description aligns with the wordmark's top. Dead centre, one photographed object (a painted wooden pepper mill about 140px wide and 440px tall) stands on a barely visible lighter rounded square with a soft contact shadow; other objects replace it in turn. Below, a centred 11px grey line, then a white rounded email field 236px wide with a circled arrow inside its right end. Roughly 80% is empty.
references.type: The wordmark is drawn lettering in a heavy display serif with tight spacing, cap height about 5.5vw. All live text is Helvetica Neue regular at 14px and about 11px, black or grey. Two text sizes only; the contrast is wordmark against near-invisible interface text.
references.colour: #f1efec #000000 #ffffff #d9261c #e8a317 #7a7a75 — Warm off-white field, black wordmark, a white input; all colour arrives through whichever object is showing (red and yellow mill, tan leather, blue cap).
references.imagery: Studio cut-outs of single everyday objects in three-quarter view with a soft grounded shadow on matching off-white, each scaled to similar visual mass and centred, one at a time, no frame.
references.layout: One fixed viewport with four elements: wordmark top-left, description top-right, object in the exact centre, form bottom-centre. Margins of 56px, no rules, nav or footer. On mobile the wordmark centres and the description disappears.

sections.description: The central object rotates through unrelated things (pepper mill, sling chair, sticker-covered hydrant, layered iced drink, record player, baseball cap), each photographed in the same light and replaced in place within a zone roughly 250-300px square. Shadow direction and visual weight stay constant, so the object is the page's only variable and no carousel controls are needed.

Beneath the object, a centred line of 11px grey text, a 30px gap, then a white field about 236 by 52px with 12px radius: light grey placeholder at left and a 26px circle-outlined arrow as the submit control inside the right end. No button label, border or shadow; the field is the only pure white on the page, which marks it as the one interactive thing.

steal: Build a pre-launch page from four elements only (wordmark top-left, one-line description top-right, a single centred object, an email field) and leave the rest of the screen empty.
Cycle one consistently lit cut-out object in the same spot to show range without adding a grid or carousel controls.
Make the email field the only pure-white element on an off-white page, with submit as a circled arrow inside it rather than a labelled button.

references.name: Transport
references.idea: Present a USB stick as a luxury object: one studio render on charcoal above a chrome custom wordmark, then let moody macro photography carry the rest.
references.hero: Flat charcoal field. Centred slightly above the midline, a cut-out render of the drive about 31% of viewport width with its steel arm swung up at 30 degrees. Under it a chrome, ultra-wide custom wordmark spans 72% of the width on one line yet is only 45px tall. Then a centred serif tagline at 2.6vw and a single row: mono spec, a dark pill showing price and sold-out state, mono spec. Logo top-left, a grey centred nav prompt, a small pill with a glowing dot top-right. Carousel chevrons sit at the far left and right edges at product height. The bottom fifth is empty.
references.type: Three voices: a chrome extended techno wordmark as image; Untitled Serif 400 at 38px with -0.026em tracking for taglines and body; ISO mono for specs and caps eyebrows. Section heads switch to a tight heavy Untitled Sans near 36px. Nothing exceeds 3.6vw.
references.colour: #1c1c1c #c8c5ba #6e6f6a #5b5d45 #f1f1ef #2d2d2d — Charcoal base with white text; colour comes only from photographs in grey-olive, concrete and amber. One section flips to dark text over a pale blurred photo.
references.imagery: One clean product render, then shallow-focus macro photographs of the translucent drive on cutting mats, concrete and fabric, graded olive-grey with grain. Full-bleed bands with feathered edges, plus a row of rounded cards of unequal widths.
references.layout: Centred hero, then full-bleed photo bands each carrying one short text group placed differently: top-left, centre-right over a card, bottom-left, centred. Band edges dissolve through heavy blur instead of hard cuts. About 160 words across eleven screens.

sections.description: Full-bleed pale out-of-focus photograph with the drive in sharp focus in the lower half. Dark text overlays the top: a heavy tight grotesk heading at about 36px, left-aligned 8% in from the edge, then three equal columns, each a tiny glyph plus mono caps label over two lines of serif copy. No cards or dividers; the photo's soft blur is the only background.

A full-width macro photo band fades out through a blurred lower edge. On charcoal beneath it, one row of four rounded-corner image cards of unequal widths (one double-width, three single) with narrow gaps, each a tightly cropped lifestyle shot in a different colour temperature. The row is cut by the viewport bottom; further down one card grows taller and pins beside a short text group.

Dark band over a concrete-wall photograph. The drive render floats at top centre, half out of frame, with a horizontal motion streak smeared across the wall behind it. Text sits bottom-left: mono caps eyebrow, heavy grotesk heading, two lines of serif. The band cross-dissolves into an olive bokeh photo holding a centred mono equation, heading and one serif line whose quantities are joined by italic conjunctions.

Two small white script-lettered badges side by side at top centre, like garment labels, with a tiny pill link beneath, then a mostly empty charcoal field. Bottom-left, three tiny stacked mono link groups; bottom-right, white card-suit icons above a two-line italic mono credit, right-aligned.

steal: Pair one centred product cut-out with a very wide, very short metallic wordmark so the logo reads as an engraved nameplate.
Give three typefaces strict jobs: serif for sentences, mono for specs and eyebrows, heavy grotesk for section heads.
Blur the top and bottom edges of full-bleed photo bands so sections melt into each other with no hard seams.
